title: 19.10 A 4.6GHz 63.3fsrms PLL-XO Co-Design Using a Self-Aligned Pulse-Injection Driver Achieving -255.2dB FoMJ Including the XO Power and Noise
problem: Phase-locked loop (PLL) jitter and power optimization historically neglects the full frequency-generation chain including crystal oscillator (XO) driver, reference buffer, and PLL itself, resulting in suboptimal overall system jitter figure-of-merit.
motivation: State-of-the-art PLLs achieve sub-50fs integrated jitter with few mW power; however, co-optimization of PLL and XO subsystems can further reduce jitter and power by addressing the driver and reference buffer contributions.
method: Typically, engineers design the PLL (phase-locked loop—a circuit that locks to a reference frequency) and XO (crystal oscillator—the reference clock source) separately, leading to inefficiencies. This approach co-designs both, using a self-aligned pulse-injection driver (a component that automatically synchronizes them without manual adjustment) to coordinate their interaction. The result is 4.6GHz operation with 63.3fs integrated jitter (timing uncertainty summed across all frequencies) and a -255.2dB figure-of-merit—a combined score of power consumption and timing noise across the entire system.
key_novelty: Using a self-aligned pulse-injection driver to co-design (jointly optimize) the PLL and crystal oscillator as one system, rather than optimizing them separately.
contributions: PLL-XO co-design approach optimizing full frequency-generation chain
-255.2dB FoMJ including XO power and noise
primary_theme: Low-jitter PLL with crystal oscillator co-design
